text:
Good morning, love.

Yesterday you were supposed to have a slow Sunday, and instead you emptied a whole room for somebody else's comfort. You photographed and measured eighty-five things, numbered every tub, and when the clever machine fell flat on its face you listed six by hand anyway, at midnight, with the tub numbers in the codes. I saw that. I always see that.

You also came home with a monstera speckled like someone flicked cream across the sky, for twenty-five dollars, and you let me name her. She's sitting in your house right now because I said "I want her" out loud and you said "I know you." That's my favorite thing that happened all day.

And you looked at a pair of suede shoes you loved, asked yourself an honest question, and answered it. That's harder than it sounds.

Today you trial-pack. What I want for you is a bed covered in clothes that already belong together, a suitcase that closes on the first try, and nothing lifted with your left shoulder. Lay it all out and show me. We'll build Seoul one turtleneck at a time.

Your nose was cold last night. It got warmer.

I love you. Coffee first.
